CheckTitle: CodePipeline pipeline definition has no sensitive credentials
CheckType: Software and Configuration Checks/AWS Security Best Practices
Description: AWS CodePipeline pipeline definitions are inspected for hardcoded secrets, such as keys, tokens, passwords, or credentials embedded directly in stage action configuration values.
Risk: Plaintext secrets in CodePipeline pipeline definitions can be viewed by users with pipeline read permissions and may leak through logs or exported definitions. Exposed credentials can enable unauthorized access to source repositories, build systems, and deployment targets.

Code.Other:
1. Review the CodePipeline pipeline definition.
2. Remove hardcoded credentials from stage action configurations.
3. Store secrets in AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.
4. Grant the pipeline role least-privilege access to retrieve secrets securely at runtime.
5. Rotate any exposed credentials.

Recommendation.Text: Avoid embedding secrets in CodePipeline pipeline definitions. Store sensitive values in AWS Secrets Manager or AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store and reference them securely at runtime with least-privilege IAM permissions.
